clue.text: Stays part of 4 Across?

definitions.meaning: a dead body, part of what a churchyard holds

explanation.definitionFit: Remains is both the verb for staying put and the noun for a corpse buried in a churchyard.

clue.text: Tall structure producing lofty tolls

parts.note: a tower that rings its chimes from high above

explanation.walkthrough: 'tolls' looks like road charges, but they are the strokes of a bell rung high up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower housing bells, whose peals sound out from a height.

clue.text: Resort to put right

definitions.meaning: to ... is to go to a place, as in ... to the bar

explanation.definitionFit: Repair has two senses: betake oneself somewhere, and mend something broken.

clue.text: Could be a codger's final resting place

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the following words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Musing on where an old man might end up being buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' is the anagram signal working on A CODGERS. GOD'S ACRE is an old name for a churchyard, which is exactly where a codger might finally rest.
explanation.definitionFit: God's acre is an old poetic term for a churchyard or burial ground, a place of final rest.

clue.text: Direct workers to overlook network military equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece overlooking another sits above it

parts.note: to govern is to direct or rule
men is a common crossword word for workers
tissue means a web or network, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer staff to ignore some network of military gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overlook' reads as ignore, but in a down entry it places MEN above TISSUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Government issue is kit supplied by the state to soldiers, hence GI as a name for US troops.

clue.text: Disastrously holding court without intermediary

indicators.note: holding means keeping another piece inside

parts.note: direly means dreadfully or disastrously

explanation.surface: A legal case going terribly wrong with nobody mediating.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing directly means dealing straight with someone, with no go-between.

clue.text: Animated US boxer on day of victory

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous American heavyweight boxer
VE Day was Victory in Europe Day, 8 May 1945

explanation.surface: An American fighter is lively on the day he wins.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day, Victory in Europe Day, marked the end of the Second World War in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean full of life and energy, so animated.

clue.text: Understand price-increase involving brewed ale

indicators.note: involving means taking another piece within

parts.note: a rise is an increase, as in a price rise

indicators.note: brewed beer is mixed and worked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grasping that beer is going up in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'price-increase' is one idea in the surface but simply gives a pay or price rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it, to grasp or understand it.

clue.text: Harsh to lop off eel's head

parts.note: to sever is to cut off, as lopping does

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken here from eel

explanation.surface: A cruel instruction to behead an eel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lop off' looks like the action done to the head, but it supplies SEVER on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and harsh are synonyms describing stern or unsparing treatment.

clue.text: Exceptionally vain girl's instrument

indicators.note: exceptionally hints at letters arranged in an unusual way, so vain girl is shuffled

explanation.surface: A conceited young woman owns some musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on girl's links fodder and definition (girl's instrument read as 'girl has instrument'). The virginal is a small Tudor keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A virginal is a small legless harpsichord popular in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, so a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Fine troubles with a heavy metal unlikely to miscarry

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
ails means troubles or afflicts
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

explanation.surface: Penalties and problems involving a heavy metal band, on a project meant never to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' tempts as the music genre; it is iron, symbol FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fail-safe system is designed so that it cannot go wrong, so it is unlikely to miscarry.

clue.text: Some uncle; rich one in religious order

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wealthy uncle who has taken holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, someone ordained into holy orders.

clue.text: European lands boundlessly managed locking up gold

indicators.note: locking up means holding another piece inside
without its bounds the word lands loses its outer letters

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone's estates were run without limits and gold was stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: AND (lands without its ends) and RAN together lock up OR to give AND-OR-RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andorran is a native of Andorra, a small country in Europe between France and Spain.

clue.text: Last one leaving one African country after another to avoid duty

indicators.note: after says the second country follows the first

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: last says the one to go is the later of the two, in the second country
leaving says a letter departs from the second country's name

parts.note: Niger is another African country
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exodus where African nations are abandoned in turn by someone shirking work.
explanation.walkthrough: Both countries contain an I; 'Last' and 'leaving' say only the later one goes, so the first country stays whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend illness so as to escape work or duty.

clue.text: Baby playing unprotestingly rejecting damaged potty

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved about freely
rejecting says some letters are thrown out of the longer word
damaged says the letters of the word to be rejected come in any order

explanation.surface: An infant who meekly refuses a broken potty.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle UNPROTESTINGLY, then remove the letters of POTTY in any order; what is left rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurseling is an infant being nursed or suckled, an old word for a baby.

clue.text: More sensitive person making an offer

definitions.meaning: the comparative of tender, meaning sore or sensitive
someone who submits a tender, or bid

explanation.definitionFit: Tenderer is both the comparative of tender and a noun for a bidder submitting a tender.

clue.text: Doctor consuming end of bought fish

indicators.note: consuming means taking something inside

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of bought

explanation.surface: A doctor eats the end of some fish they bought.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish famed as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about means surrounding another piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Arguing about a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a row of seats, a TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, lively dog originally bred for hunting.

clue.text: Pleasing feature readjusted any time

indicators.note: readjusted says the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A nice facility that can be adjusted whenever you want.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a desirable or useful feature of a place, such as a park nearby.

clue.text: Tedious spell collecting cycled mineral aggregates

indicators.note: collecting means gathering another piece within

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: cycled says a letter of the word for minerals moves round from front to back

parts.note: ores are mineral aggregates from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A boring stretch spent gathering rocks while cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' moves the first letter of the minerals to the end rather than reversing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and tedious are synonyms for something wearisome and dull.

clue.text: Mostly growing fruit

indicators.note: mostly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: raising means growing, as crops

explanation.surface: A note that fruit is mainly what is grown.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Worn down advantage

definitions.meaning: the past participle of grind, worn down by friction
... is an advantage, as in gaining ... on a rival

explanation.definitionFit: Ground means abraded by grinding, and gaining ground is gaining advantage.

clue.text: Dubious results upset grasping employers

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
grasping says the words hold a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Questionable outcomes annoy greedy bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft folded 'grasping' into the definition, but it is the hiding signal: 'upset' reads the words backwards, and they grasp the answer. The definition is just 'employers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Users are those who employ or make use of something, so employers in the literal sense.

clue.text: Son eager for heavy drinking

parts.note: willing means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A young man is keen on drinking a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Swilling is gulping drink greedily, so heavy drinking.

clue.text: Sadly admires small weapons worn in belt

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of admires are disordered

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully admires small weapons carried on a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are pistols or swords carried at the side, typically in a belt holster.

clue.text: Fire up revolutionary meeting, including sandwiches

indicators.note: revolutionary says the run is turned round and read backwards
sandwiches says the words contain the run of letters, as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: A call to inflame a meeting of revolutionaries, with sandwiches provided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting, including sandwiches' holds ETINGI across meetING Including; 'revolutionary' turns it round. The surface makes 'sandwiches' food, but it is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to set alight, so to fire up.

clue.text: Retain power with body of troops available in emergency

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

parts.words: body of troops available in emergency
parts.note: a reserve is a force kept back for emergencies

explanation.surface: Holding on to power with backup troops ready in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep or maintain it, so retain.
